name: system_requirements
title: Query the system requirements for a package (and its dependencies)

origin.description: Returns a character vector of commands to run that will install system requirements for the queried operating system.
origin.usage: system_requirements(os, os_release = NULL, path = ".", package = NULL, curl = Sys.which("curl"))

arguments.name: os, os_release
arguments.text: Operating system name and release. If os_release is NULL, os must be name and release separated by one dash, such as "ubuntu-18.04". A unique prefix is accepted. The names are ubuntu, centos, redhat, opensuse, and sle.

arguments.name: path
arguments.text: Path to the package root. Used when package is NULL. The directory must contain a DESCRIPTION file.

arguments.name: package
arguments.text: CRAN package name or names. When not NULL, path is ignored.

arguments.name: curl
arguments.text: Path to the curl binary. The default is Sys.which("curl"). An empty string is refused after the operating system is checked.

origin.details: The call posts to the Posit Package Manager sysreqs API. RSPM_ROOT defaults to https://packagemanager.posit.co and RSPM_REPO_ID defaults to 1. A DESCRIPTION file is sent with --data-binary and suggests=true. Package names use a query with all=false and pkgname repeated. An error field in the response stops with that text. pre_install commands come first, then install_scripts, each made unique.
origin.value: A character vector of commands. Empty when the package has no system requirements.
origin.example:
pkg <- tempfile()
dir.create(pkg)
writeLines("Package: testPkg\nSystemRequirements: libcurl", file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))
cmd <- system_requirements("ubuntu", "16.04", pkg)
cat(sprintf("system_requirements(\"ubuntu\", \"16.04\") for SystemRequirements: libcurl returns \"%s\".\n", cmd))

translation.description: Returns the commands that install system requirements for the queried operating system.

arguments.name: os
arguments.text: Operating system name, or "name-release" when os_release is None. A unique prefix is accepted. An ambiguous or unknown name stops with match.arg's message.

arguments.name: os_release
arguments.text: Release, such as "16.04" or "7". None splits os on "-" into exactly two pieces. A trailing empty piece is dropped once, as in strsplit.

arguments.name: path
arguments.text: Package root used when package is None. A missing DESCRIPTION stops with "`<path>` must contain a package."

arguments.name: package
arguments.text: One package name, or a list of names. None posts the DESCRIPTION file. Names use the query form, with pkgname repeated and all=false.

arguments.name: curl
arguments.text: Path of the curl binary. None uses the first curl on PATH. An empty string stops with "`curl` must be on the `PATH`." after the operating system check.

translation.details: RSPM_ROOT defaults to https://packagemanager.posit.co and RSPM_REPO_ID defaults to 1. The DESCRIPTION form sends the file with --data-binary and suggests=true. The package-name form does not. curl is run through sh -c the way system2 does. The body is parsed like remotes' json$parse, so a backslash-n in an error stays two characters. pre_install is collected before install_scripts. Each list is made unique, then they are concatenated. A command object contributes its values, including command.
translation.value: A list of command strings. An empty list when the package has no system requirements.
translation.example:
import os
import tempfile
from remotes.system_requirements import system_requirements
pkg = tempfile.mkdtemp()
with open(os.path.join(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    handle.write("Package: testPkg\nSystemRequirements: libcurl\n")
cmd = system_requirements("ubuntu", "16.04", pkg)
print(f'system_requirements("ubuntu", "16.04") for SystemRequirements: libcurl returns "{cmd[0]}".')
